source.facts: Confirmed by Winston (Nov 2026): co-founder and only designer; the other seven were developers; he made product calls and handed off designs; Nov 2022 – Jan 2025; A2–A4 sections are closest to v1.0 (iOS, Nov 2024; also on Android); live timing shipped and detected delays automatically from posted results; tournament mode exists because you don't need those features outside an event, other features help you find teams and tournaments then, and its UI is built for the fast-paced tournament environment (own experience + tester input); your own next match leads with the time because time is what you act on (own experience competing + user/team feedback); the 2023 plan's organizer portal, chatbot and web app gave way to priorities; the ScoutSheet tab (A5) shipped in a later update; TeamSync, Groups and the new onboarding (A5/R1/R2) were designed but not shipped; feedback after launch led to fixes only; 4,000+ accounts; 4.8-star rating; '3x faster' came from automated tests clicking through competitor apps vs Elapse to reach the same data. Takeaways he chose: design for the moment; ship the core first; live data needs honest states.

fields.description: A tournament companion for VEX Robotics teams: next match, live schedule and scouting. 4,000+ accounts.
fields.intro: After four years competing in VEX Robotics, I co-founded Elapse to put a team’s next match, live schedule and scouting in one app. I was the only designer, working with seven developers.
fields.summary: How might we help robotics teams know when and where their next match is, even when the schedule runs late?
fields.overview: As co-founder, I made product calls and handed off designs to seven developers. Elapse launched on iOS in November 2024 and is also on Android.

sections.title: Problem
sections.heading: Tournament day moves fast
content: I competed in VEX Robotics for four years. At every tournament, the same things got in the way:

bullets: The official schedule app took several taps and spread information across screens.
Schedules weren’t updated when matches ran late.
Announcements over the mic were easy to miss.

sections.title: Plan vs. release
sections.heading: From plan to release
content: The 2023 plan was bigger than what we launched. We focused on what teams needed most.

bullets: **Planned:** an organizer portal for delays and announcements, a chatbot, and a web app for phones, tablets and computers.
**Shipped in v1.0:** tournament mode, upcoming matches and live timing.
**Designed, not shipped:** team sharing and a new onboarding.

sections.title: Next match
sections.heading: Your next match comes first
content: Home leads with your next match: number, alliance teams, field and time. On your own match, the time and “In X minutes” come first. Other matches lead with the match number.

bullets: **Time is what you act on:** it tells you when to head to the field.
**It came from competing,** and teams told us the same.

gallery.alt: Elapse home with a next match card showing match Q23, alliance teams, field and time, and upcoming matches below
Elapse Your Next Match screen leading with a large time and In X minutes
Elapse Match Info screen for another match leading with the match number

content.caption: Home, your next match (time first), another match (number first).

sections.title: Live timing
sections.heading: Delays you can see
content: Matches often run late. Live timing worked out delays from when results were posted and updated the schedule on its own.
Instead of quietly changing the time, the app shows the new time with “Delayed – originally …”. Finished matches show “Started 3 mins late”.

gallery.alt: Elapse next match screen showing the new time with Delayed, originally and the old time
Elapse match screen for a finished match: You won!, Started 3 mins late, scores and ranking changes

content.caption: A delayed match, and a finished one that started late.

sections.title: Tournament mode
sections.heading: A mode for tournament day
content: The Events tab and live schedule live in a tournament mode you turn on at the event. It switches off afterwards.

bullets: **You don’t need it outside an event.** Other features help you find teams and tournaments then.
**Its UI is built for a fast-paced day** at the event.
**It came from my own experience** and from testers.

gallery.alt: Elapse home before an event with a tournament card and a Tournament Mode button
Elapse tournament rankings opened as a separate screen outside tournament mode
Elapse rankings inside the Tournament tab while tournament mode is on

content.caption: Turning it on from home, and rankings outside vs. inside tournament mode.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.heading: What shipped and what I learned
content: Elapse reached 4,000+ accounts with a 4.8-star rating. In our automated tests, reaching the same data was about 3x faster than in competing apps. After launch, feedback mostly led to fixes rather than design changes.
ScoutSheets came in a later update: specs, photos and notes on each team’s page.

gallery.alt: Elapse team page with a Scoutsheet tab and a Create Scoutsheet button
A filled Elapse ScoutSheet with robot specs, photos and notes

content.caption: A team’s ScoutSheet, empty and filled.

bullets: **Design for the moment.** Tournament day leaves little attention, so the next match has to read at a glance.
**Ship the core first.** Leaving the portal and chatbot out let us release what teams needed.
**Live data needs honest states.** Show a delay next to the original time instead of hiding it.
